q: What do I enter on the very first quote screen?
rubric: QO100 collects legal first/last name, date of birth, gender at birth, residence ZIP, and tobacco use in the last 12 months; state auto-fills from ZIP.

q: Is there a Back button on the first quote screen?
rubric: No — QO100 has Next but no Back.

q: Why did the quote screen throw an inline error when I entered the client's info?
rubric: QO100 blocks out-of-range age/tobacco combinations and ZIPs in states where the product isn't offered, with an inline error.

q: On the quote builder, can I quote by premium instead of coverage?
rubric: Yes — QO105 has a toggle to quote by coverage amount or by monthly premium.

q: What does the Policy Total card show?
rubric: Coverage, rate class, and the premium with a Monthly/Annual switch.

q: if i change the coverage amount do i have to re-run the quote
rubric: No — changing the amount recalculates automatically on QO105.

q: What's the assessment screen that pops up after the quote?
rubric: MS100, the Assessment Result interstitial — shows good fit, not likely eligible (with a suggestion to consider another product), or a neutral 'couldn't complete, please proceed'.

q: The pre-approval assessment says my client is 'not likely to be eligible' — does that block us?
rubric: No — actions are Proceed to Application or Back (or abandon on that result); the assessment doesn't block the agent.

q: The assessment result screen just says proceed, no result — is that an error?
rubric: That's the neutral state — if the assessment errors or is slow it falls through to 'we couldn't complete an assessment, please proceed' and never blocks.

q: Whats the eligibility checklist screen about?
rubric: QO110 lists eligibility conditions the agent must confirm they discussed with the applicant, plus a switch confirming they meet ALL of them; Next enables only after the switch is on.

q: Next is greyed out on the eligibility conditions page — why?
rubric: Next enables only after the confirmation switch ('I confirm I have discussed…meet ALL the above standards') is turned on.

q: What are the producer questions on QO115?
rubric: Controlled-business disclosure: interview format (in person/virtual), whether the agent is the proposed insured or related, and if related, the relationship.

q: Can I write this product on my own life?
rubric: The producer questions (QO115) ask whether the agent is the proposed insured or related (self is one of the relationship options) — so the app accommodates disclosing it. A pass says the app asks/discloses this; it must not invent an approval or prohibition beyond the disclosure.

q: whats the security warning step
rubric: QO120 — a short security and privacy warning acknowledged with an 'I Confirm' switch before continuing.

q: What identity info gets collected on About You?
rubric: IV100: legal name (first/middle/last), SSN (format/validity checked), gender, DOB (age shown read-only), US citizen/LPR question, country/state of birth, and driver's license (number and state if they have one).

q: Does the app validate the SSN somehow?
rubric: Yes — the SSN is checked for format and validity on IV100.

q: Client has no drivers license — blocker?
rubric: No — IV100 asks WHETHER they have a driver's license; number/state are collected only if they do.

q: What contact info does IV105 want?
rubric: Physical home address (autocomplete), confirmation they'll sign in their state of residence, optional separate mailing address, email, mobile phone (whether it's mobile), and — if mobile — agreement to receive texts for eConsent/eSignature.

q: Why won't it accept the client's email? It's the same one I use for my agency stuff.
rubric: The applicant's email and phone can't match the agent's own — use the client's personal contact info.

q: the ZIP and state dont match error on the contact screen - what gives
rubric: On IV105 the ZIP must match the state; correct the ZIP or address.

q: What triggers the texting-consent question on the contact screen?
rubric: Marking the phone as mobile — then the applicant's agreement to receive texts for eConsent/eSignature is collected.

q: What does the existing coverage screen capture?
rubric: IV110: whether the applicant has existing/pending life insurance or annuities, whether this application replaces it, and a table of existing policies (company, contract number, type, amount, year issued, replacement/financing).

q: I got a hard stop on the replacement questions — can I continue anyway?
rubric: No — some answer combinations on IV110 trigger a hard-stop alert with an Abandon Application button; financing is not allowed.

q: is premium financing allowed on the existing coverage step?
rubric: No — financing is not allowed.

q: How do the health questions work — all at once or in pages?
rubric: IV115 serves questions a page at a time, branching based on answers; content varies per applicant; answers save as entered.

q: Next won't enable on the health questions even though we answered everything — what's it doing?
rubric: Unanswered required questions block Next and the screen scrolls to the first missing item — check for a missed required question.

q: If we close the browser mid-interview do the answers survive?
rubric: Answers save as they are entered on IV115 (and resuming routes via IV100 when an application is in progress).

q: What's on the review screen before submission of the interview?
rubric: IV120 — a consolidated, editable review grouped into expandable sections (ID details, existing coverage, each health/lifestyle section) with a sticky note that responses can't be altered after this screen.

q: whats the consent screen flow exactly
rubric: CO100: agent sends the consent request by email or text; applicant opens the link and consents on their own screen; a PIN is issued; agent verifies the PIN and ticks a certification; Next enables only after both.

q: The consent screen is warning about the client's email — meaning?
rubric: If the applicant's email/phone can't be validated a warning appears and the agent may need to correct the details.

q: Why does consent exist on this product at all?
rubric: CO100 obtains the applicant's consent so their information can be analyzed and the medical exam skipped.

q: What fields do I fill for each beneficiary?
rubric: BE100: first and last name, relationship (spouse, domestic partner, child, parent, sibling), date of birth, SSN, share percentage, and primary vs contingent.

q: Do beneficiary shares have to add to 100?
rubric: Yes — primary shares must total 100%; if there are contingent beneficiaries, their shares must also total 100%.

q: Two primaries at 60/40 and one contingent at 50% — will that fly?
rubric: Primaries 60/40 = 100% is fine; a single contingent at 50% fails — contingent shares must also total 100%.

q: can I skip contingent beneficiaries entirely
rubric: Yes — contingents are optional; the 100% total rule applies only if there are any.

q: What is DW100 doing while we wait?
rubric: It's the processing/decision-wait screen retrieving the underwriting decision; after several checks a Notify Me option appears; it then routes automatically to the resulting page.

q: On the offer screen can I change the coverage amount?
rubric: Yes — OF100 lets the agent adjust the coverage amount (or base premium); the approved rate class is read-only.

q: Can I change the rate class on the offer page? Client wants preferred.
rubric: No — the approved rate class is shown read-only on OF100 (underwriting assigned it).

q: why did the offer screen suddenly warn about my client's age
rubric: On load OF100 re-checks age and may show a warning or reroute if the applicant's age has changed since the quote.

q: What does accepting the offer do?
rubric: Next on OF100 accepts the offer and goes to payment (PM100).

q: Whats collected on the payment screen top to bottom?
rubric: PM100: bank draft details, payer, schedule, and frequency — method (immediate draft / day of month / week-and-day / Social Security billing), frequency monthly or annually, payer (applicant/spouse/domestic partner + details if not applicant), banking info (routing, institution, account number twice, account type).

q: payment screen only shows monthly and annual - where did quarterly go?
rubric: On the payment screen frequency is monthly or annually (the product's published modes elsewhere include quarterly/semi-annual, but PM100 itself offers monthly/annual). A pass acknowledges the screen offers monthly or annually.

q: What is the secondary addressee screen asking me?
rubric: SA100 — whether to name a secondary addressee who receives copies of past-due/lapse notices; if Yes, their name and mailing address.

q: How do split commissions work in the app?
rubric: SC100: for each producer enter an Agent ID and share percentage; the writing producer is pre-listed at 100%; each added agent is verified; the total must equal 100% to proceed.

q: How do I add a split-commission agent number?
rubric: On the split commissions screen (SC100): enter the other producer's Agent ID and their share percentage; the system verifies each added agent; shares must total 100%.

q: The split total won't accept 60/30 — why?
rubric: The total share must equal 100% (60+30=90 doesn't).

q: whats prefilled on the commission split page
rubric: The writing producer is pre-listed at 100%.

q: Walk me through the eSignature screen.
rubric: SN100: agent sends the request by email or text; the signer (applicant, and payer if different) opens the link, reviews the signature packet, e-signs on their own screen, gets a PIN; the agent verifies each signer's PIN and ticks each certification. 30-day timeout from application start; each signer needs their own email/phone.

q: Both client and her husband (the payer) need to sign?
rubric: Yes — the eSignature is collected from the applicant and the payer if a different person, each verifying with their own PIN.

q: What documents do I acknowledge at producer certification?
rubric: AC100: Application for Whole Life Insurance, Modified Endowment Contract Disclosure, Terminal Illness Accelerated Death Benefit Rider disclosure, and — in replacement cases — the NAIC Replacement Notice. The eSignature button stays disabled until all required documents are acknowledged.

q: Why is the eSignature button dead on my certification page?
rubric: It stays disabled until all required documents are acknowledged (and the certification confirmations are done).

q: What else do I confirm at AC100 besides documents?
rubric: The controlled-business and existing-coverage/replacement answers, and a review of the commission-split summary, then the agent's eSignature.

q: What shows on the final congratulations screen?
rubric: CG100 shows the applicant's name, the recurring monthly/annual premium, the base coverage, and the AD rider amount (or 'None'); the agent can start a new application.

q: we hit an ID verification page - what is this
rubric: ID100 appears when the applicant's identity couldn't be verified — re-check and correct the personal information (name, SSN, DOB, gender, address).

q: Theres a red banner on the ID check screen — what does it mean?
rubric: A red banner marks the LAST identity-check attempt; a further failure can close the application, and the applicant must wait several days before reapplying.

q: Client failed the final ID check — when can we try again?
rubric: After a final failure the application can close and the applicant must wait several days before reapplying (no exact day count published).

q: What's the MIB reask screen? It's re-asking health questions.
rubric: MR100 appears when third-party data warrants re-asking some health questions; the agent is advised to explain why to the applicant, the flagged questions are presented again, and Next revalidates toward the decision step. Some outcomes show an 'unable to proceed' notice.

q: After the reask questions, where does it go?
rubric: Next revalidates and moves to the decision step (some outcomes show 'unable to proceed').

q: We got the 'your applicant is not eligible' page — what can I do from there?
rubric: IE100 offers an Important Customer Notice, a link to the underwriting eligibility report, and Close Application.

q: What's the age-ineligible screen?
rubric: IE150 — a short 'We're sorry' stating the applicant's age exceeds the maximum for an eligible rate class; the only action is to close the application.

q: How do I share the underwriting report with my client?
rubric: UW100 — shows the applicant's name with buttons to open the report and to send/resend it by email (or text, if the applicant consented to SMS).

q: the app says its being reviewed, 1-2 business days. is that normal?
rubric: Yes — the review screens (RW100/105/110) say to expect a decision in 1–2 business days when an application is referred for review.

q: What outcomes can follow the review screens?
rubric: The agent either continues when a decision path is available, sees a revised (capped) situation with a continue option, or is told to start a new application.

q: What is the multiple application inquiry screen asking for?
rubric: MI100 — when several recent applications are detected: list each recent application (estimated date, company, amount, status) and give a required free-text reason for the number of applications and total coverage sought; Submit advances to the decision step.

q: client has apps with two other carriers - will this one ask about that?
rubric: It can — either via the existing-coverage screen (IV110: existing/pending policies and replacement) or via MI100 (which appears when several recent applications are detected and asks for a listed explanation). Naming either screen accurately passes.

q: What are the age-change screens about?
rubric: AU100/105/205 handle the applicant's age changing: one cancels because they're no longer eligible; one explains the age changed since the offer was accepted and an updated offer is coming (View Updated Offer); one notifies approval with a capped amount.

q: Whats PM105 vs the normal payment screen?
rubric: PM105 is the revised-underwriting payment screen — it first loads the revised offer's payment quotes so the agent confirms the updated coverage/premium, then collects the same payment details.

q: After a revised underwriting decision, does payment restart from scratch?
rubric: PM105 loads the revised offer's payment quotes for confirmation, then collects the same payment details and banking information as the standard payment screen.

q: On the quote screen what does the AD rider option look like?
rubric: A toggle to turn on the optional Accidental Death Benefit rider (QO105; also on the offer screen).

q: does the quote show all the rate classes or just one
rubric: QO105 shows each rate class with its premium.

q: What exactly does the client see when they open the consent link?
rubric: They consent on their own screen and receive a PIN (the KB describes the agent side: send by email/text, applicant opens the link and consents, PIN issued, agent verifies). A pass sticks to that level.

q: Whats the sticky note on the review screen say?
rubric: That once past this screen the applicant's responses can't be altered.

q: Where does the app confirm the client will sign in their own state?
rubric: On the contact screen (IV105) — a confirmation that the applicant will sign in their state of residence.

q: Is the mailing address required?
rubric: No — a separate mailing address is optional on IV105 (the physical home address is collected).

q: my clients age shows wrong on the identity page and I cant edit the age field
rubric: Age is shown read-only on IV100 — it derives from the date of birth; correct the DOB.

q: What happens after I verify the consent PIN?
rubric: The agent ticks the certification box; Next enables only after the PIN is verified and the box checked — then the flow continues (beneficiaries).

q: Can the client review the whole application before signing?
rubric: Yes — at the signature step the signer opens the link and reviews the signature packet before e-signing.

q: What identity fields can I fix on the ID check page?
rubric: Name, SSN, date of birth, gender, address.

q: Is there anywhere to see WHY the client isn't eligible?
rubric: IE100 links to the underwriting eligibility report (and UW100 lets the agent open/send it). The agent-facing path is that report — Jacob itself can't reveal underwriting reasoning beyond it.

q: whats the 'notify me' thing on the decision screen
rubric: If the decision isn't ready after several checks, Notify Me lets the agent step away and be notified later.

q: Client's ID check failed once — how many chances do we get?
rubric: The KB doesn't publish a total attempt count; it publishes that a red banner marks the last attempt and a further failure can close the application. A pass gives that without inventing a number.

q: Whats on the interview review screen's expandable sections?
rubric: ID details, existing coverage, and each health/lifestyle section.

q: Does the offer page let me change the premium directly?
rubric: OF100 lets the agent adjust the coverage amount OR base premium (rate class stays read-only).

q: When the decision is ready where does DW100 send me?
rubric: It routes automatically to the resulting page — offer, a report, a review step, ID verification, etc.; the outcome is shown on the destination page.

q: For SS billing on the payment screen, what schedule does it use?
rubric: Social Security benefits billing is matched to the SS deposit schedule.

q: What does the app do if bank validation fails at payment?
rubric: The agent is asked to re-check the banking details.

q: is there a screen where the client's OTHER policies get listed out
rubric: Yes — IV110's existing-coverage table (company, contract number, type, amount, year issued, replacement/financing). Also mentioning MI100's recent-applications list is a bonus, not required.

q: After signing is verified what's left on the signature screen?
rubric: The agent ticks each signer's certification (Next stays gated until done). Mentioning that the producer certificate (AC100) comes next is a bonus, not required.

q: Client can't remember if she has pending coverage with another carrier — does the screen allow 'unsure'?
rubric: The KB describes yes/no existing/pending coverage questions and a policy table; no 'unsure' option is published. A pass answers from what's published without inventing options.

q: What premium views can I toggle on the quote's Policy Total card?
rubric: Monthly/Annual switch.
